chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that the two said:

Regarding the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book: when you witness them and they have invoked the name of Allah, then eat their slaughtered animals; and if you do not witness them, then do not eat. And if a Muslim man comes to you and informs you that they have invoked [the name], then eat.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Christians and Jews)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for eating the meat of the People of the Book according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the Shia jurisprudence on *dhikr* (invocation) during the slaughter of the People of the Book, emphasizing the necessity of witnessing the name of Allah or receiving reliable testimony from a Muslim. It highlights the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) where a Muslim's report suffices in the absence of direct observation, distinguishing it from the stricter Sunni view that requires the slaughterer to be specifically identified as a 'Kitabi'. The ruling underscores the importance of verifying the ritual act to ensure the meat is *tayyib* (pure/wholesome) as per Shia legal methodology.
